meta.description: One place where every conversation becomes text and a written summary: calls made through any IP PBX, meetings held in Zoom, Teams or Meet, and recordings you already have and simply drop in. Windows, macOS and Linux. Your recordings and your AI can stay on your own machine. Free software under GPL v2.
hero.eyebrow: Free software · GPL v2 · Windows, macOS and Linux
hero.title: You talk. It listens, writes it down, and tells you what matters.
hero.sub: Calls, meetings, and recordings you already have. All of them transcribed, written up and filed the same way.
hero.lead: Three ways in for a conversation, and the same treatment for all three. Place or take the call here — a proper business phone, on any IP PBX you already have. Sit in a meeting in Zoom, Teams or Meet and it is recorded from the computer itself. Or drop in a recording made somewhere else entirely. However it arrived, it is kept, turned into text you can search, and written up — the summary, the tasks, the category — without anybody typing.
hero.note: Windows, macOS and Linux. No account, no subscription, no cloud service in the middle — see how it works.
hero.fact1: calls, meetings, and files you already have
hero.fact2: calls, text and AI can stay on your machine
hero.fact3: free software, no licence per seat
hero.fact4: a complete interface in every one of them
how.title: From any conversation to a written summary, with nobody typing it up
how.lead: Four steps. You are only involved in the first one.
how.s1.p: Three ways in, and after this step it no longer matters which one it was: a call you place or take here, a meeting running in Zoom, Teams or Meet on the same computer, or a file you already have and drop in.
how.s2.p: A call or a meeting is recorded on two channels, you on one and the far side on the other, so who said what is never in question — and the way the other party is told about it is yours to set. A file you brought in is a recording already, and goes straight to the next step.
how.s3.p: The recording is transcribed on its own, turn by turn, in the language it was spoken in. Click a line and hear it. Search a year of calls by what was said in them.
how.s4.p: A summary, the tasks the call left you, the subject it was really about, the things worth flagging — and a box where you can simply ask the conversation a question.
feat.title: The product as it stands
feat.lead: From the conversation arriving to the write-up it leaves behind — and the settings, the integrations and the diagnostics underneath.
feat.f13.h: Any conversation, whichever way it arrived
feat.f13.p: What matters here is what happens to a conversation afterwards, not where it came from. Three ways in, one library: the same recording, the same transcript, the same write-up, and one search across all of it.
feat.f1.h: Everything you expect from a business phone
feat.f1.p: Register as many lines as you have, run several calls at once, and move them around the way the day demands.
feat.f2.p: Choose your headset by the name your computer shows it under, ring on the speakers while you listen on the headset, and hear that it works before the first call rather than during it.
feat.f3.p: Recording runs by itself, with you on one channel and the other party on the other, so what each side said is never in doubt.
feat.f11.p: A conversation in Zoom, Teams, Meet or anything else is recorded from the computer itself — the far side from what the machine is playing, you from your own microphone — and lands in the same library, transcribed and written up like everything else.
feat.f4.h: Conversations you can read, and search
feat.f4.p: Every recording becomes text, speaker by speaker, kept in step with the audio — click a line and hear the moment it came from.
feat.f5.p: As soon as there is a transcript, the phone reads it and files it: what the call was about, what was decided, and what it left you to do. Every one of these is a template you can open, reword and put back.
feat.f6.h: Your AI, wherever you keep it
feat.f6.p: The phone talks to the model you choose — one running on your own hardware, or a service you already pay for — and tells you what it is costing while it does.
feat.f7.h: Always on, out of the way
feat.f7.p: Close the window and the phone stays on the line: it sits in the tray, tells you who is calling, and answers a hotkey while you are working in something else.
feat.f8.h: Contacts and history, beside the phone
feat.f8.p: Your address book and your call log stand next to the dialler, and a number that belongs to somebody shows their name everywhere it appears.
feat.f9.h: Fits the software you already run
feat.f9.p: Three ways in, from no code at all to a couple of lines of it, and each one off until you want it. An afternoon of work rather than a project — the integration page walks through all of it.
feat.f10.p: Passwords live in the keychain your operating system already trusts. Recordings, transcripts and history live in a file you own. Nothing about a conversation — not a number, not a name, not a word of what was said — goes anywhere you did not send it yourself.
feat.f12.p: The product is a small core with its capabilities beside it rather than built into it. Turn one off and it is gone — no settings page for it, no menu entry, nothing of it running.
lang.title: The interface in thirty languages, the conversations in any
lang.lead: English and twenty-nine others: each of them a complete interface rather than a half-translated one, chosen in the settings and changed without a restart. What language a call was spoken in is a separate question — the transcript and the write-up follow whatever was actually said.
int.home.title: Your software controls the calls. The softphone reports back.
int.home.lead: The simplest way to get CTI integration up and running in minutes. A local REST API and built-in webhooks generator. Enable only when you need them. No SDK, no intermediary cloud service, and no externally exposed network listener.
ps.home.title: Every conversation, written up your way.
ps.home.lead: Start with 11 ready-made prompts, then change the words, the criteria and the rules to fit the way you do business. Your LLM, your key, your control.
